title: Hypercontractivity on Finite Product Spaces
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$. Assume $0<\lambda\le1$, every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$, $q>2$, and $\rho\ge0$ with $\rho\le \lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$. Then every real-valued function $f$ on the product space satisfies both $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights
Every coordinate atom has weight at least $\lambda$
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $\lambda$, where $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q>2$. For $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$ and every $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
